profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Software Engineer at Google.

Previously, SRE for 4+ years at Google.

Previously, full-stack software engineer with 4+ years of Python/Django experience and a focus on building developer tools and infrastructure. Extremely fast learner and a fearless debugger with a natural drive to solve tough problems.

positions.title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer
positions.description: https://landing.google.com/sre/

company.name: The University of Texas at Austin

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Develop MuleSoft APIs for both our home-grown financial crosswalks system and the cash sales reporting component of our upcoming ERP system, and maintain our new MuleSoft API for UT's centralized receivables system.

Establish standards and conventions for new technologies coming online as part of the university-wide transition to a new ERP system. Help determine best practices for departmental usage of new tools such as git, GitHub, Artifactory, and Zenoss.

Analyze legacy code and design replacements for financial systems that will not be covered by the new financials ERP, but must be converted away from legacy hardware.

Write educational materials and help develop curriculum for early-career software developers and developers with less web development experience in our department to teach best practices and topics relevant to the work in our department. Will soon serve as a mentor for an early-career developer working through this month-long curriculum.

Lead development and maintenance of our financial crosswalks system.

Lead regular maintenance of several Python/Django and JSP applications, as well as internal libraries shared by many of the Django applications. Lead efforts to keep our 30+ web applications and libraries up-to-date, as new versions of Django and other third-party libraries are released.

Maintain UT's centralized credit card processing infrastructure (Java). Worked with the payment processor, clients of our REST API, and end users to keep the system available and reliable.

Served as a Python/Django challenge analyst for a Software Developer trainee.

Full-time remote worker in Seattle since September 2015.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
Led development of a legacy-to-future crosswalk system, to provide a central location for mapping financial concepts and entities in UT's current financial system to their equivalents in our upcoming ERP system.

Wrote educational materials and helped develop curriculum for early-career software developers and developers with less web development experience in our department to teach best practices and topics relevant to the work in our department.

Proposed, designed, and led implementation of an internal tool for code repository management, for our 70+ code repositories.

Led upgrades of ~30 Django applications and libraries from Django 1.7 to Django 1.8.

Led regular maintenance of several Python/Django and JSP applications, as well as internal libraries shared by many of the Django applications. Led efforts to keep our 30+ web applications and libraries up-to-date, as new versions of Django and other third-party libraries are released. Promoted the adoption of automated testing and continuous integration with Jenkins in the department.

Acted as the primary steward for the Request Forms System. Led and provided mentorship for the development of new forms in this system. Developed a new payment request form for this system.

Maintained UT's centralized credit card processing infrastructure (Java). Worked with the payment processor, clients of our REST API, and end users to keep the system available and reliable.

Served as a Python/Django challenge analyst for a Software Developer trainee.

Nominated for the 2015 Cathy Lester Rising Star Award.

Continued on as a full-time remote worker with FIS when I moved to Seattle in September 2015.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Spent a week familiarizing myself with Java to become a steward of UT's central credit card processing system. Developed a Swing application to serve as a testing tool for the CC system's REST API.

Became the primary steward for the Request Forms System. Provided guidance and mentorship for the development of several new HR-related forms in this system.

Led efforts to upgrade shared JavaScript and Python code to accommodate changes to UT's single-sign-on service.

Led upgrades of ~30 Django applications and libraries from Django 1.4 to Django 1.7.

Served as a Python/Django challenge analyst for two Software Developer trainees.

Served on the TADS Environment Management committee. (See TADS description in Projects section.)

Nominated for the 2014 Cathy Lester Rising Star Award.

positions.title: Software Developer/Analyst
positions.description:
Led development of the Travel Reimbursement Request in the Request Forms System. Wrote and tested lots of custom JavaScript to make the add-expense functionality very user-friendly.

Led a 3-hour workshop on running an Oracle database in a Vagrant environment for ~30 members of the UT developer community. Have provided support for the example environment (utvms) ever since.

Fixed bugs related to UT's custom web- and mainframe-based financial management system.

Learned how to maintain some small Java applications.

Served as a Python/Django challenge analyst for two Software Developer trainees.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Worked as core team member for the development of the Request Forms System and its first two forms.

Designed and developed a Python/Django/Oracle application for moving the Excel-based, fixed asset tracking system online. Worked very closely with clients to deliver a system that met their annual reporting needs.

Fixed bugs related to UT's custom web- and mainframe-based financial management system.

Served as a Python/Django challenge analyst for three Software Developer trainees.

positions.title: Software Developer Trainee
positions.description:
Learned to develop and maintain administrative applications in the UT environment, including writing NATURAL/Adabas programs for mainframe database access and developing Python/Django applications for administrative web interfaces.

Developed a code review packet generation program in LaTeX, with automatic updating of mainframe-based code snippets.

positions.title: Pre-Doctoral Fellow
positions.description:
I was enrolled in the astronomy Ph.D. program at the University of Florida as a Graduate Fellow, where I TA'd for three semesters and worked with Dr. Jian Ge on characterizing the compositions of stars in the MARVELS exoplanet survey.  

In the Spring of 2011, I taught two sections of an introductory astronomy laboratory course where I gave short lectures about basic topics in astronomy, assisted students in the completion of their labs, and led them through observations at a real telescope.

In the Fall of 2011, I was a TA for an introductory class about the search for life in the universe, and my duties included holding office hours to answer questions about the content and structure of the course, grading homework sets and extra credit, and proctoring exams.

In the Spring of 2012, I was the TA for a more general introductory astronomy course, and my responsibilities were to hold office hours each week and review sessions before each of the exams.

positions.title: Physics TA and Graduate
positions.description: I taught an introductory physics lab and staffed an astronomy resource room and student observatory as a TA in the Department of Physics and Astronomy.  I stayed at UNL during this time as a physics MS student in order to compete in my final year of track and field.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Designed and tested self-healing, thin membranes using piezoelectric transducers and acoustic waves to detect and seal micro-cracks in the membrane. Developed both the systems to be tested and the procedures with which to test. Collected and analyzed data, wrote Agilent VEE Pro programs to automate testing procedures, and provided general assistance to other groups in the lab. Worked on this project as an NSF REU student in the summer of 2006.

company.name: South Dakota School of Mines and Technology

positions.title: REU Research Assistant
positions.description: Analyzed historical data to help correlate the mass-loss rate of Asymptotic Giant Branch stars with their metallicities. Used Python and IDL to analyze historical observations to plot and fit light curves to measure pulsation periods and amplitudes of these AGB stars.

projects.title: Request Forms System
projects.description:
The Request Form System is a Web-based system, which allows university employees who do not have authorization for administrative systems to initiate a request. Requests can then be assigned to one or more employees who can take any number of actions including: update, approve, assign, decline, or finalize. When the request is finalized, it generates an electronic document in the appropriate system (e.g., *DEFINE) or an email to the appropriate office to notify the department of an action(s) that must be taken.

The Request Form System is designed to reduce duplication of effort by decreasing the amount of data entry required on the part of administrative staff and to increase the accuracy of request initiation.

Types of forms in RFS include travel authorization requests, purchase requests, travel and entertainment reimbursement requests, and HR-related requests. Each form has a unique set of fields, validations, and JavaScript behavior.

projects.title: Technology Architecture Design and Specifications
projects.description: Research and analyze available product solutions in order to define a component-based, administrative systems architecture that is flexible, predictable, resilient, secure, and scalable. Allowing University developers to focus their IT skills on solving business problems, not figuring out architecture, tools, and environments.
